description: A three-node Keel cluster. Every panel here answers a question somebody actually asks during a demonstration: who is leader, is it replicating, is it durable, and did anything break. Panels are described rather than left to be guessed at, because a dashboard whose numbers need explaining out loud is a dashboard that gets screenshotted and misread.

panels.description: One line per node, 1 when it believes it is leader. Two lines at 1 in the same term would be an Election Safety violation; two at 1 in *different* terms is a deposed leader that has not found out yet, which is normal and brief. The distinction is the term panel below.
panels.title: Who is leader

panels.description: Terms only ever increase. A term climbing while nothing else moves is a cluster that cannot elect - a partitioned node campaigning, or a quorum that is not there. Pre-vote exists to keep this flat.
panels.title: Term

panels.description: How far each node is behind what the cluster has committed. Two distances, because they fail differently: applied-behind-commit is a slow state machine, durable-behind-commit is a slow disk, and only the second one costs a leader its ability to count itself towards a quorum.
panels.title: Replication lag

panels.description: Committed entries per second, derived from the index rather than from a counter, so it is the same quantity the safety oracles watch.
panels.title: Commit rate

panels.description: 1 when this node's fsyncs survive power loss. A cluster showing 0 here is running in a mode no durability claim may be made about, and every benchmark taken against it is refused by the Publishable gate for the same reason.
panels.title: Durability

panels.description: Voting members. It changes during a membership change and the nodes disagree about it briefly, which is joint consensus working rather than failing.
panels.title: Configuration size

panels.description: 1 when a node has hit a storage error it cannot continue past. It stops serving rather than carrying on, because a node that cannot make writes durable and keeps acknowledging them is worse than a node that is down.
panels.title: Latched storage failure

panels.description: Segment files on disk. A count that climbs and never falls is compaction not happening - the log floor is not moving, which eventually means a restart replays everything.
panels.title: Log segments

panels.description: Entries per Ready: how many operations one round of persist, replicate and apply served. This is the first number to look at when writes are slow. One entry per Ready means every operation is paying a whole round on its own, whatever it was told about batching — that is what a hundred writes a second looked like, while the same cluster at a batch of thirty did four thousand.
panels.title: Batch size

panels.description: Proposals the core turned away before they reached the log — not the leader, overloaded, or a configuration change already in flight. A client sees these as retries and nothing else on this dashboard shows them at all.
panels.title: Proposals refused

panels.description: Payload bytes per second in the resumable snapshot stream. A receiver line returning after a process restart is the transfer resuming rather than beginning again.
panels.title: Snapshot transfer

panels.description: Mean time to checkpoint and durably move the log floor. This is the synchronous stall PR-6 limits; a rising line says checkpoint creation, not network transfer, is holding the node loop.
panels.title: Checkpoint stall

panels.description: End-to-end committed-command latency measured from admission to the committed response. Refusals and retries are excluded.
panels.title: Commit latency p99

panels.description: The durable-sync portion of a Ready. Compare this with commit latency to distinguish storage pressure from consensus or apply pressure.
panels.title: Fsync latency p99

panels.description: Distribution of entries sharing one Ready. This directly verifies that batching is occurring instead of inferring it from aggregate counters.
panels.title: Ready batch distribution

panels.description: Observed replication messages outstanding per follower. A sustained value at the configured ceiling identifies flow-control pressure.
panels.title: Follower in-flight window

panels.description: Real election campaigns started by each node. Pre-vote attempts are intentionally excluded; spikes correspond to availability events.
panels.title: Elections

title: Keel
